findings.reason: The protected Python solution reverses the character array in-place in two steps: first reversing the entire array s, then scanning for space delimiters and reversing each individual word in-place. The algorithm runs in O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space; no candidate is required.
Reversing the whole array reverses both word ordering and character order within words; reversing each word locally restores character direction while leaving inverted word ordering intact.

The full-array reversal takes O(n) swaps, and individual word reversals perform at most O(n) total swaps, yielding O(n) total time. Auxiliary space is O(1) for loop indices. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Accepts list of single-character strings s, mutating s in-place and returning None.

The approach accurately details 2-layer reversal composition (full array reversal followed by per-word reversal), in-place pointer swapping, space delimiter detection, and O(n) time / O(1) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover string splitting storage overheads, word shift quadratic costs, call stack space trade-offs, single-word inputs, and single-space delimiter guarantees.
